correctness.rationale: For each shared word, the image of the full product is the Cartesian product of the two image sets. A shortest common reset is therefore the first singleton pair reached by BFS on the 49 nonempty subset pairs; if both components reset, concatenation gives a common reset, irrespective of strong connectivity. The proof domain is all 3^6 complete transition tables per component on the same ordered alphabet, without quotienting the spectrum. The independent cutoff-free exhaustive BFS reproduced 549 synchronizing components, with 153,324,48,24 at thresholds 1–4 and 180 nonsynchronizing; for 301401 ordered synchronizing pairs it reproduced 13041,154008,87552,37872,7488,1440 at lengths 1–6. Independent state conjugations, common letter swap and factor swap give exactly 11 length-six orbits (nine of 144 and two of 72). The sharp ordered individual profiles are (3,4):576, (4,3):576, (4,4):288. The printed witness baabab resets the displayed pair and BFS rules out shorter words for it. Inspected the source Python and C++ certificates and both recorded outputs without executing uploaded code. The separate Python reproduction works using only its standard library.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial small product regime is natural in shortest-reset theory: three-state factors already have distinct individual thresholds and the naive compositional upper bound is eight. The exact census resolves how a shared word delays resetting, measures how often the worst case occurs, and classifies the extremal pairs up to the natural symmetries. These are concrete benchmarks one may need for product bounds, not an isolated sampled witness or a re-count of the individual automata.
